text: Can an insurer lose money on insurance and still make a profit?
From July to September, ICICI Lombard's insurance lost three hundred and eighteen crore rupees.
Yet its profit after tax was nine hundred and forty six crore.
The difference is the float. Premium comes in first. Claims are paid later. Meanwhile, the money is invested.
Investments held against policyholders' money earned one thousand one hundred and sixty one crore in the quarter.
On the company's own chart, the industry's insurance lost money in each of the last ten years. So the real test is the combined ratio.
Float helps. The combined ratio decides how much. Which brings us back to the question.
